subject: Connecting points in paired measurements study

messages.author: 291801e42ec308cd
messages.subject: Connecting points in paired measurements study
parts:
Guys

Sorry for the newbie question. Tried to find the answer in past emails but got no luck.

I have the dataset, from a paired observations study:

   id      status         dt
1  17         BCR  56.530887
2  17 SRT failure   4.581458
3 122         BCR   8.581850
4 122 SRT failure 100.000000
5 125         BCR   5.471255
6 125 SRT failure  14.008240

which I plotted using:

ggplot(data, aes(x=status, y=dt)) + geom_point(size=4,colour="#000000",position=position_jitter(width=0.05))

So, now I would like to connect the dots. Is it possible to do with only this data ? Or I will have to calculate an intercept and slope for each variable and use the geom_abline() function ? Is there any other better function ? Geom_segment() maybe ?

Thanks

Roberto

One small sample dataset:

structure(list(id = c(17, 17, 122, 122, 125, 125), status = structure(c(1L, 
2L, 1L, 2L, 1L, 2L), .Label = c("BCR", "SRT failure"), class = "factor"), 
    dt = c(56.5308871179212, 4.58145814023428, 8.58185033458939, 
    100, 5.47125543964156, 14.0082396570109)), .Names = c("id", 
"status", "dt"), formats = c("%9.0g", "%11.0g", "%9.0g"), types = c(255L, 
251L, 255L), val.labels = c("", "Status", ""), var.labels = c("masterid", 
"", ""), version = 10L, label.table = structure(list(Status = structure(c(1, 
2), .Names = c("BCR", "SRT failure"))), .Names = "Status"), row.names = c("1", 
"2", "3", "4", "5", "6"), class = "data.frame")

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Connecting points in paired measurements study
parts:
Hi:

I think this is the idea you're after. I put in colors for individual
IDs, but if you have a large number of them, it may well be better to
just stick with basic black. I'll show an example with and without
jittering to show you why you shouldn't jitter if you want to 'connect
the dots'.

df <- structure(list(id = c(17, 17, 122, 122, 125, 125), status =

structure(c(1L,
2L, 1L, 2L, 1L, 2L), .Label = c("BCR", "SRT failure"), class = "factor"),
dt = c(56.5308871179212, 4.58145814023428, 8.58185033458939,
100, 5.47125543964156, 14.0082396570109)), .Names = c("id",
"status", "dt"), formats = c("%9.0g", "%11.0g", "%9.0g"), types = c(255L,
251L, 255L), val.labels = c("", "Status", ""), var.labels = c("masterid",
"", ""), version = 10L, label.table = structure(list(Status =
structure(c(1,
2), .Names = c("BCR", "SRT failure"))), .Names = "Status"),
row.names = c("1",
"2", "3", "4", "5", "6"), class = "data.frame")

position=position_jitter(width=0.05)) +
geom_line(aes(group = id))

# (2) Plot without jittering, colored by ID
# Use factor(id) for color to map individual colors to IDs
ggplot(df, aes(x = status, y = dt)) +
geom_point(aes(colour = factor(id)), size=4) +
geom_line(aes(group = id, colour = factor(id)))

In paired studies, it is often useful to plot one response against the
other, each (x, y) pair corresponding to a single respondent. One
qualitative measure of the efficiency of pairing is that the higher
the correlation between the response pairs across respondents, the
more 'efficient' is the paired design vis a vis an unpaired design. To
generate such a graph from the data, just recast it and then produce
the scatterplot:

dfm <- cast(df, id ~ status, value = 'dt')
ggplot(dfm, aes(x = BCR, y = `SRT failure`)) +
geom_point(size = 4, color = 'black')

By using a colour aesthetic on the points, you can generate a legend
of IDs; alternatively, you could use geom_text() or the directlabels
package to label each point by ID. Clearly, the more pairs you have,
the less you would want to do this; OTOH, you may want to label
unusual points, in which case you could create a subset data frame for
them and then pass it into geom_text().

Hope you find something useful in this,
Dennis
